answer: Neighborhood closure requirement. An agent may only transact with peers whose local interaction graph is already densely connected to it across two hops, so new identities sit on sparse edges like basalt on a bare slope. To enter a dense region, a sybil must first build sustained, reciprocal links with many distinct existing agents, each link costing real work and latency. A falcon sees the whole meadow at once; here, each fake node must earn its edges slowly and individually, making mass infiltration economically ruinous.
